# For Reed Richmond, Comparing Medicare Plans Is an Annual Routine — and eHealth Makes It Simple


When Reed Richmond retired five years ago, he


encountered


a


common


problem


among


many


newly eligible Medicare


beneficiaries


.


“I had plenty of Medicare options, but I didn’t have a way to compare them side by side,” said


Reed


,


70


, who retired after a


career in public health education


.


Then the Ohio resident learned about eHealth.


Reed went online and discovered he could compare Medicare Advantage plans based on the


factors


that mattered


most


to him


—


from costs and benefits to his doctors and prescription medications.


“


I


t was so simple,” he said. “You could compare what was covered and what wasn't and what the rates were.”


Five years later, Reed is still using eHealth


every fall


.


While he is


happy


with his


current


Medicare coverage


,


Reed


wants to make sure


he


stays that way


.


**From four plans to one**


Reed's first experience with eHealth was entirely online.


He started by looking at plans from four insurance companies. Using


eHealth’s


MatchFinder


tool


, he narrowed those options to two.


“The thing that was so convenient was having all the plans laid out side by side,” Reed said.


That allowed him to evaluate his choices using his own healthcare priorities rather than trying to make sense of different plan materials individually.


But Reed


didn't


stop once he selected a plan.


E


ach


year since


, he has returned to eHealth to check his Medicare Advantage coverage against the alternatives available to him.


“I do it every year


a


t


the end of October


to make sure I’m in the best plan for me


,” he said.


**Why checking every year matters**


For Reed, that annual review


isn't


simply an exercise.


A couple of years ago, it led him to change plans.


He found that costs under his existing coverage had increased and that the plan


wouldn’t


provide the prescription coverage he needed


to treat a heart condition


.


Changing plans


reduced


Reed’s copay by


$15


per month,


an amount that


could add up to hundreds of dollars over the years to come


.


“Paying nothing each month is better than paying something,” Reed said.


The experience reinforced something


he


had already begun to understand: The Medicare Advantage plan


that's


right for you today


isn't


guaranteed to remain the right one tomorrow.


Plans can change. Prescriptions can change. Doctors can change. Most importantly, a person's health can change.


**Combining technology with a human second opinion**


While


Reed is comfortable comparing Medicare plans online, when he changed coverage a few years ago, he wanted another level of reassurance before making the decision.


H


e called eHealth and spoke with a licensed insurance agent.


“It was nice to talk to someone live rather than just looking at a screen,” Reed said.


The agent listened to what Reed was looking for and helped narrow the available choices.


More importantly, she helped


validate


what Reed had already discovered online.


“She


verified


all the things I was looking at were correct,” he said.


That combination works well for Reed. He can research and compare plans himself, then speak with someone when he wants


additional


confidence before making a


final


decision.


“Now that I've used it, I feel confident,” he said.


**Advice Reed shares with friends**


Reed's experience has made him an informal Medicare resource among friends approaching retirement.


When they ask how he navigated his choices, his recommendation is straightforward.


“My friends


call


me and


ask


how I did it,” Reed said. “And I tell them, ‘Go to eHealth.’”


-


** This story reflects the customer’s actual experience. He was compensated with a $15 gift card for his time.*
